- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75); adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until trend reverses.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong downward momentum, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5 days; if sentiment is neutral, maintain baseline.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to reflect sentiment bias.
